chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from 'Ali ibn al-Salt, from Zur'ah, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

When you intend to enter into ihram on the Day of Tarwiyah, then do as you did when you intended to enter ihram: trim your moustache, clip your nails, and remove from your pubic hair if you have hair; pluck your armpits, perform ghusl, and put on your two garments. Then go to the mosque and perform six rak'ahs there before entering ihram, and supplicate to Allah and ask Him for help, and say—then he mentioned the supplication.

key_terms.أَظْفَارِكَ: your nails, which are to be clipped before ihram
key_terms.الْعَوْنَ: divine help and assistance sought from Allah
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque, where the prayer is to be performed before ihram
key_terms.تُحْرِمَ: to enter into the state of ihram for hajj
key_terms.شَارِبِكَ: your moustache, which is to be trimmed as part of preparation
key_terms.يَوْمَ التَّرْوِيَةِ: the eighth day of Dhu al-Hijjah, when pilgrims prepare for hajj rites

ai.seo_question: What should a person do before entering ihram for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah?
ai.summary: This hadith outlines the recommended preparations for entering into ihram for hajj on the Day of Tarwiyah. It includes acts of bodily grooming, ritual purification, wearing the garments of ihram, performing salat, and making du'a before entering the state of ihram.
